label: <DEL> delimiter step in long (L>=8) sequences
explanation: Low end of candidate unit 72 fires mainly at the <DEL> delimiter step: 77% of activation mass, 71% of active steps, and every top example. The rate rises steeply with sequence length (t=8/9, i.e. delimiter steps of L=8/9 sequences, hold about 77% of mass; L=9 alone holds 52%). It fires on only ~24% of L>=8 delimiter steps, though. Which ones depends on sequence content: sequences rich in m, x, h, y, q and digits 0/1/3 fire more (adding a count of these tokens raises dev F1 only from 0.35 to 0.40, so this was not adopted). Weaker secondary activity appears on the first copy outputs (recall_idx 1-3) and the final output of L=9 sequences. It is almost never active during the original input phase (<1% of mass), and it does not fire at delimiter steps of short sequences (L<=6).
